polite_rewrite: Hi Adam, I hope you had a good weekend. You mentioned replying about the brand kit by Friday, so I wanted to check in. Is there anything you need from me to decide?
explanation: Referencing their own promised date makes the chase factual, not pushy.

input: I sent the landing page draft a week ago and the client has not reviewed it. The project is stalled.
polite_rewrite: Hi Chloe, the landing page draft has been waiting for review for a week now. Could you take a look when you have a chance? Once approved, I can finish the remaining work quickly.
explanation: Linking review to finishing the work gives the client a reason to act.

input: I want to check in with a client I have not heard from in three months about the dashboard.
polite_rewrite: Hi Leo, it has been a while! I hope you are doing well. I wanted to check in and see how the dashboard is performing. If you need any updates, I am here.
explanation: A friendly check-in after months keeps the relationship alive.

input: Client has not replied to my last two messages about the video edit. I need a final check-in.
polite_rewrite: Hi Maya, I have messaged a couple of times about the video edit without hearing back. I wanted to check if the project is still on. If your plans changed, no worries, just let me know.
explanation: A graceful closing option respects a client who has moved on.

input: I need to follow up on a contract for the e-commerce store that the client has not signed yet.
polite_rewrite: Hi Sam, I wanted to check if you have had a chance to review the contract for the e-commerce store. I am happy to answer any questions about it. Once signed, I can start right away.
explanation: A contract follow-up with a start promise encourages signing.

input: Client said they will decide on the social media campaign next week. I want to stay top of mind without pestering.
polite_rewrite: Hi Nadia, thanks for the update on the social media campaign. I will check back next week as planned. In the meantime, I have attached a recent sample you might like. No need to reply now.
explanation: Sharing a sample adds value instead of just asking for a decision.

input: I need to follow up on an unpaid invoice for the report for the third time.
polite_rewrite: Hi Owen, this is my third follow-up on the overdue invoice for the report. I understand things get busy, but I do need a payment date this week. Could you confirm one by Friday?
explanation: Counting the follow-ups calmly justifies asking for a firm date.

input: I sent the quote for the presentation ten days ago and the client went quiet. I need to nudge them.
polite_rewrite: Hi Ruby, I hope you are well. I sent the quote for the presentation ten days ago and wanted to check if you had any questions about it. I am happy to adjust the scope if needed.
explanation: Offering to adjust the scope gives a quiet client a reason to reply.

input: The client asked for the product photos quote but has not replied in two weeks. I want to close the loop.
polite_rewrite: Hi Felix, I wanted to check if the product photos quote is still of interest. If your plans changed, no worries at all. Just let me know either way so I can plan my schedule.
explanation: A close-the-loop message with a graceful exit respects a silent client.

input: I need to follow up with a client who promised to send the deposit for the email template last Monday.
polite_rewrite: Hi Aisha, I hope you are well. You mentioned sending the deposit for the email template last Monday. Could you let me know when it will arrive? Once it does, I will start right away.
explanation: Referencing their own promised date makes the chase factual, not pushy.

input: The client said they loved the chatbot demo but has not replied to my proposal in a week.
polite_rewrite: Hi Carlos, I am glad you loved the chatbot demo! I wanted to check if you had a chance to look at the proposal. I am happy to walk through it on a short call if that helps.
explanation: Referencing their enthusiasm plus a call offer keeps the follow-up warm.

input: I want to check in with a client after delivering the online course to see if students like it.
polite_rewrite: Hi Elena, I hope the online course is going well with your students! I wanted to check in and see how it is performing. If you need any tweaks, I am here.
explanation: A post-delivery check-in shows care beyond the invoice.

input: The client has ignored my last three messages about the newsletter. I need to decide whether to close the project.
polite_rewrite: Hi Viktor, I have messaged three times about the newsletter without hearing back. I will close the project for now. If you would like to continue later, just let me know and we can pick it up.
explanation: Closing the project cleanly with a reopen offer respects a client who has gone silent.

input: I want to introduce myself to a new client for the podcast cover for the first time.
polite_rewrite: Hi Hana, thank you for the invitation. I am a designer with four years of experience, and your podcast cover sounds like a great fit. I would love to learn more about your goals.
explanation: A warm self-introduction with relevant experience opens a new client conversation.

input: Client just hired me for the UI kit and I want to send a welcoming first message.
polite_rewrite: Hi Lucas, thank you for choosing me for the UI kit! I am excited to get started. I will send a short kick-off plan today so we are aligned from day one.
explanation: Excitement plus a kick-off plan makes a new hire feel confident.

input: I need to say hello to a client I have not spoken to in a year about the SEO audit.
polite_rewrite: Hi Nina, it has been a while! I hope you are doing well. I was thinking about our last SEO audit and wanted to check in. How is it performing?
explanation: A warm check-in after a year revives the relationship naturally.

input: I want to wish a long-term client a happy Eid after finishing the motion graphics project.
polite_rewrite: Hi Tara, wishing you a very happy Eid! Thank you for a wonderful project on the motion graphics. I look forward to what we build next.
explanation: A seasonal greeting with thanks strengthens a long-term bond.

input: I need to welcome a client to the pitch deck kick-off meeting.
polite_rewrite: Hi Victor, welcome! Thank you for joining the kick-off for the pitch deck. I am excited to walk you through the plan today and hear your thoughts.
explanation: A welcoming kick-off greeting makes the client feel included from the start.

input: Client messaged me on a Saturday about the animation. I want to reply politely on Monday morning.
polite_rewrite: Hi Wendy, good morning! Thanks for your message about the animation. I have had a look and will get back to you with a full reply by this afternoon.
explanation: A Monday-morning reply acknowledges the message without apologising for the weekend.

input: I want to congratulate a client on winning an award after our 3D render project.
polite_rewrite: Hi Yusuf, congratulations on the award! It has been a pleasure working on the 3D render with you. Wishing you many more successful years ahead.
explanation: A milestone congratulation shows care beyond the project.

input: I need to say hello to a client on Telegram for the first time about the copywriting project.
polite_rewrite: Hi Ibrahim, great to connect here! I am working on your copywriting project. Feel free to message me anytime during work hours.
explanation: A casual Telegram hello fits the channel while staying professional.

input: I need to cancel a meeting about the data dashboard with a client at short notice.
polite_rewrite: Hi Fatima, I am sorry, but I need to cancel our meeting about the data dashboard today. Something urgent has come up. Could we reschedule for tomorrow? I apologise for the inconvenience.
explanation: A short apology plus a reschedule offer softens a late cancellation.

input: I need to ask a client for a testimonial after the successful membership site launch.
polite_rewrite: Hi Bilal, I am so glad you are happy with the membership site. If you have a moment, a short testimonial would mean a lot to me. Even a few sentences would help.
explanation: A testimonial ask after success feels natural and low-pressure.

input: I need to reschedule a call about the event poster with a client to next week.
polite_rewrite: Hi Hassan, would it be possible to move our call about the event poster to next week? I am free Tuesday or Thursday afternoon. I apologise for the change and hope one of those works.
explanation: Offering two new times makes rescheduling easy.

input: The client wants me to sign an NDA before we discuss the brand guidelines project.
polite_rewrite: Hi Sara, I am happy to sign the NDA for the brand guidelines. Please send it over and I will return it signed today. Once that is done, we can discuss the project freely.
explanation: A quick yes to an NDA with a same-day promise builds trust.

input: I need to tell a client I am going on holiday during the app icon set project and who will cover for me.
polite_rewrite: Hi Ali, I wanted to let you know I will be on holiday next week during the app icon set project. My colleague Sam will cover anything urgent. I will be back on Monday and will catch up then.
explanation: Early notice plus a named cover person keeps a holiday smooth.

input: I need to send a client the final invoice for the mobile game UI and thank them.
polite_rewrite: Hi Zainab, thank you for a great mobile game UI project! I have attached the final invoice. It has been a pleasure working with you, and I hope we collaborate again soon.
explanation: Pairing the final invoice with thanks ends the project warmly.

input: I need to apologise for sending the wrong attachment about the resume design to a client.
polite_rewrite: Hi Hamza, I am sorry, I attached the wrong file for the resume design. The correct one is attached here. Please delete the earlier file. Thank you for your understanding.
explanation: A quick correction with a delete request fixes a wrong attachment.

input: Client wants me to teach them how to update the wedding invitation themselves.
polite_rewrite: Hi Noor, I would love to show you how to update the wedding invitation. I can record a short video guide, or we can do a one-hour training call. Which would you prefer?
explanation: Two teaching options let the client pick their preferred learning style.

input: I need to politely end the menu design project with a client because it is no longer working out.
polite_rewrite: Hi Rayan, after thinking it over, I feel it is best to wrap up our work on the menu design here. I will finish the current milestone and hand over everything cleanly. Thank you for the opportunity.
explanation: A clean handover offer makes ending a project professional, not abrupt.

input: I need to let a client know I am fully booked for the next month and cannot start the course slides yet.
polite_rewrite: Hi Dina, thank you for reaching out about the course slides. I am fully booked for the next month, but I have availability from the 1st. Would you like me to reserve a slot for you?
explanation: Fully-booked news plus a future slot turns a no into a booking.
